contexts.text: Everything... ascribed to chance, or to fortune, is of Providence... The Divine Providence works so invisibly... in order that a man may in freedom ascribe it either to Providence, or to chance.

There was a certain one who had confirmed himself in this, that nothing is of the Divine Providence, but everything is from prudence, also from fortune and chance. (His experience after death.) Under Fortune, see this reference. There is no such thing as chance. To the Divine they ascribe only a universal government; all the rest they call fortune, or chance.
They refer all things to sagacity, and what they do not refer to sagacity they refer to fortune, or to chance.
They who trust in their own sagacity attribute to themselves all things which turn out well for them, and all the rest they ascribe to fortune, or to chance.

And God cause it to come to his hand () = appearing as chance, as is evident from the idea of chance among the ancients, which was that it happened from God, wherefore they expressed chance by saying that God caused it to come to the hand...
That accidents or chances are of Providence, References.
There is no chance, that is, no evil happens by chance...
The Angels of the interior Heaven do not so fully believe that all things come forth from the Lord... wherefore they admit chances; but the Angels of the more interior Heaven admit no chances...
That there is no chance I have been instructed by many experiences.
